messages.text: Merson: Arsenal didn't make X factor signing to win Champions League

metadata.summary: Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level.
metadata.content: Arsenal didn't make X factor signing like Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez to win Champions League, says Paul Merson | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Arsenal didn't make X factor signing like Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez to win Champions League, says Paul Merson Paul Merson gives his verdict on Arsenal's Champions League hopes in his latest column; Sky Sports pundit believes Gunners needed more than Kai Havertz up front; Follow Napoli vs Arsenal on the Sky Sports app with our dedicated match commentary from 6.30pm on Wednesday Paul Merson Football Expert & Columnist @PaulMerse Wednesday 9 September 2026 13:50, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson has his say on whether Arsenal will have a chance at claiming Champions League glory. Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level. They have enough to win the Premier League with their squad. I just think the forward line against the big boys, they're missing that little ingredient. If they'd had a Vinicius Junior or a Julian Alvarez, that would have given them the edge to go on and win the Champions League. I think they might just fall short. Antonelli joined the Mercedes junior programme as an 11-year-old after some remarkable results in karting and quickly rose up the motorsport ranks to Formula 1 and replaced Lewis Hamilton at the Silver Arrows only last year. He currently leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from team-mate George Russell ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid and is on course to become the youngest world champion in F1 history at 20 years old. messages.text: Shelton beats Alcaraz at 3.33am in New York epic

metadata.summary: Ben Shelton clinched the biggest win of his career as he defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set epic stretching deep into the New York night to reach the semi-finals of the US Open.
metadata.content: US Open: Ben Shelton beats Carlos Alcaraz in five-set thriller in latest-ever finish to US Open match at 3.33am | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Ben Shelton beats Carlos Alcaraz in five-set thriller in latest-ever finish to US Open match at 3.33am Ben Shelton clinches first-ever victory over top-three opponent as he beats Carlos Alcaraz to set up US Open semi-final showdown with Frances Tiafoe; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app Wednesday 9 September 2026 12:37, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the thrilling US Open quarter-final between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz Ben Shelton clinched the biggest win of his career as he defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set epic stretching deep into the New York night to reach the semi-finals of the US Open. The American prevailed 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) over four hours and 28 minutes to reward a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd gripped until 3.33am in what was the latest-ever finish to a US Open match. It marked Shelton's first career win over a top-three player, against which he had been 0-17 coming into the match. Shelton will now play Frances Tiafoe in the final four after his fellow countryman's thrilling five-set victory over Alex Michelsen earlier in the evening. metadata.content: Spanish GP: What to expect from new Madring track in Madrid with Carlos Sainz predicting safety cars and red flags | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Spanish GP: What to expect from new Madring track in Madrid with Carlos Sainz predicting safety cars and red flags The Madring street circuit in Madrid is set to be a huge challenge for the drivers as Formula 1 enters the unknown this weekend; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 8 September 2026 14:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oracle Red Bull Racing swapped the asphalt for the underground, as the iconic RB8 took to the tracks of the Madrid Metro in a first-of-its-kind stunt Formula 1 has a brand-new track to look forward to this weekend and the expectation is there will be carnage and the drivers will be seriously tested at the Madring. The Spanish Grand Prix has moved from its traditional circuit in Barcelona to a high-speed street track in Madrid and has been described as "Jeddah on steroids" by Formula 3 drivers who tested there last month - the Jeddah track itself is one of the most challenging circuits in F1. So why is the Madring so difficult and how will it impact the racing we see this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1 ? metadata.summary: Jamie Carragher believes Erling Haaland will be the "best goalscorer of all time" after his double earned Manchester City a 2-0 win at Porto in the Champions League.
metadata.content: Erling Haaland: Jamie Carragher believes Manchester City striker will be greatest goalscorer of all time | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Erling Haaland: Jamie Carragher believes Manchester City striker will be greatest goalscorer of all time Erling Haaland scores double in Man City's win at Porto in Champions League; Haaland has now hit 364 goals for top-flight clubs and country in his 424-game career; Jamie Carragher tells CBS Sports: "I just can't see Haaland not scoring 1,000 goals or being the best goalscorer of all time" Wednesday 9 September 2026 12:43, UK Image: Erling Haaland scored twice in Man City's Champions League win at Porto Jamie Carragher believes Erling Haaland will be the "best goalscorer of all time" after his double earned Manchester City a 2-0 win at Porto in the Champions League. Haaland's brace in Portugal saw him become Man City's third-highest goalscorer of all time, taking his tally to 167 in just 203 appearances, and he is now 93 goals behind record-holder Sergio Aguero. The 26-year-old has hit 364 goals for top-flight clubs and country in his 424-game career - and Carragher has backed the Norway international to become a record-breaker.
